verdicts.strongest_argument: The underlying fact is not obscure by any measure: NOAA published the July 2026 CONUS record (76.9F, warmest month in the 1895-present record, all states in the warmest third) on 2026-08-10 and it was front-page national news the same day at NBC, CBS, PBS and Axios. Cooling-degree-day sensitivity is standard sell-side practice across the HVAC-adjacent complex, and the trade press ran the service-call consequence explicitly through June and July (ACHR News, 'Longer Heat Waves, Bigger HVAC Challenges'; local coverage of contractors running 6-7 calls per tech). ServiceTitan's fiscal calendar is public, so 'the record month is the last month of the quarter' is arithmetic anyone can do. What I could NOT find published is the specific transmission to the disclosed line item: no preview of tonight's print connects record cooling load to usage revenue or the payments take-rate on GTV. Every preview I found frames the quarter on Max/agentic AI, enterprise mix and operating margin. So there is a genuine residual, but it is a residual on a headline macro fact, and the arithmetic caps it hard. The weather-variable line is usage revenue, $58.5m of $268.8m in Q1 (21.8%, not 25% - professional services of $8.3m is implementation work and is not weather-driven, so the hunter's $66.8m non-subscription figure overstates the exposed base by about a seventh). Against a Q2 guide of $284-286m, only the July slice of usage (~$23m) was unknown when guidance was set on 2026-06-04; a 5-10% weather uplift on that slice is $1.1-2.3m, or 0.4-0.8% of revenue, on a name that already beat by 4.7% in Q1. Real, but a small share of a 10.08% implied move.

prior_publication.what_it_says: NOAA NCEI: July 2026 CONUS averaged 76.9F, warmest month in the full record, every state in the warmest third and none near or below average.
National wire coverage of the same NOAA release the day it was issued.
Second national outlet carrying the record-hottest-month finding.
HVAC trade press covering the direct consequence for contractors - longer heat waves, more emergency service calls - during the quarter itself.
Trade press forecast of high July heat pressure across the US, published before the month began.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Nothing in the tape looks like a weather trade. Spot 84.645 with run_up_5d -13.66% and pct_from_52w_high -29.24% on no company-specific news I could find; the sector context is the 2026 AI-agent derating of per-seat SaaS. Skew 25d +5.14 vol points means the paid direction is downside, and a bullish end-market claim is therefore contrarian to the priced lean rather than agreeing with it - which argues against a high number. But the run-up is a sector-multiple move, not an end-market move, so the absence of a weather bid is weak evidence that weather is unpriced: it is more likely evidence that weather is not what tonight is about.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A preview or sell-side note published before tonight that explicitly models July cooling degree days into ServiceTitan's usage revenue or GTV would push this to 85; conversely, management quantifying a weather contribution to a Q2 usage beat larger than ~2% of total revenue would pull it to 40.

verdicts.strongest_argument: This is a headline BLS release from 2026-09-02, six days before the print, carried by Construction Dive, ENR, Yahoo Finance and NAHB's Eye on Housing. There is no version of JOLTS that is obscure. But the more damaging point is that the transmission is largely broken, and the sources that published it say so themselves. First, the composition: ENR and Construction Dive both attribute the July strength to data-center and power construction, with data-center construction up 46% year over year. JOLTS 'construction' is the whole supersector - heavy and civil, nonresidential building, and specialty trade - and ServiceTitan sells to residential and commercial *service* contractors in HVAC, plumbing, electrical and roofing. A data-center construction hiring boom adds close to zero ServiceTitan seats. Second, hires is a gross monthly flow, not a headcount stock; the finding gives no separations figure, so a 14.7% m/m jump in hires is consistent with elevated churn and a flat technician base, which is what a seat-billed subscription line actually tracks. Third, timing: July is the last month of the quarter, so even a real seat gain contributes at most one month, against contracted subscription terms that were largely booked earlier. Subscription revenue was $202.0m in Q1; a 1% one-month seat lift is about $0.7m, roughly 0.25% of revenue. Fourth, net dollar retention above 110% already embeds seat expansion in the guide. And fifth, the interaction that matters: the market's live worry about this name is that the $245-400 per-technician-per-month seat model is what AI agents disrupt. A JOLTS print showing more technicians does not answer the question the multiple is being cut on.

prior_publication.what_it_says: BLS JOLTS for July 2026, the primary release, free and universally followed.
Construction hires 366,000 (+14.7% m/m, +9.9% y/y), openings 326,000, highest rate in nearly two years.
Same JOLTS data, and attributes the strength to data-center construction up 46% y/y - i.e. not ServiceTitan's residential trades end market.
NAHB's own writeup of the same July construction openings series.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: JOLTS landed 2026-09-02 and TTAN fell over the following sessions (-4.7% on 09-04 per Daily Political, and a further leg to 84.645 by 09-08, 5d -13.66%). If anything the tape moved the wrong way for this claim on the day it was published, which is consistent with the stock trading on the software-multiple narrative and not on construction labour at all. Put/call OI ratio 0.13 with 25d skew +5.14 says protection is being bought without a large put book - a positioning tell about AI/software risk, not about technician headcount.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: A residential-trades-specific employment series (BLS specialty trade contractors employment, or ServiceTitan's own disclosed active technician count) showing a July step-change of the same magnitude would raise the size estimate materially and drop this toward 50.

verdicts.strongest_argument: Both legs of this comparison are wire copy from the same day. Watsco's release is dated 2026-07-29 (globenewswire path /2026/07/29/, matching the EDGAR exhibit the hunter cites) and the '+5% domestic residential HVAC equipment, +2% units, +2% ASP' line is in the release body under a headline that literally reads 'Further Industry Stabilization'. It was picked up by Modern Distribution Management, ACHR News, HVACR Trends and Yahoo Finance within a day. Lennox reported the same morning, 2026-07-29 - the finding says '30-July', which is one day off - with Home Comfort Solutions revenue -7% to $936m on -12% units, and the divergence-versus-commercial framing was itself published (Investing.com, 'Lennox Q2 2026 slides: commercial strength offsets residential slump'). So neither the datapoint nor the contrast is unpublished; the word the market has been given for the residential end market since 29 July is Watsco's own word, 'stabilizing'. I also checked the AHRI series the brief warned me about, and the hunter is right to have discarded the stale 2025 figures: the current data is June 2026 shipments of 1,023,571 units, +21.7% y/y, with first-half 2026 +3.0% - published in trade press in August 2026 and supportive of the claim, though June 2025 was a depressed A2L-transition comp so the +3.0% half-year figure is the honest one. Two things keep this from being a 90. Watsco's quarter ends 30 June, so it covers only two of ServiceTitan's three months and misses the record July entirely. And the market's read of the Watsco print was negative - shares sank 15% on gross margin down 180bp - so the bullish residential-volume line inside a release the tape sold is arguably underweighted by consensus. That is a real but second-order point, and it is a defence against a bear cross-read rather than a source of upside. Note also that both series are equipment-unit series and ServiceTitan monetises job count and GTV, so the mapping is loose in both directions - which cuts against the finding as much as for it.

prior_publication.what_it_says: Watsco Q2 release, headline claims 'further industry stabilization'; domestic residential HVAC equipment sales +5% with +2% units and +2% ASP.
Trade press summary of the same release, headlined on demand stabilizing.
HVAC trade coverage of Watsco's stabilization message.
Lennox Q2: Home Comfort Solutions revenue -7% to $936m on -12% unit volume, FY EPS guide cut to $23.00-24.00 from $23.50-25.00. Note the date is 29 July, not 30 July as the finding states.
Published framing of the Lennox print as a residential slump offset by commercial - i.e. the company-specific-versus-industry distinction was already in the coverage.
AHRI June 2026 shipments 1,023,571 units, +21.7% y/y; first-half 2026 +3.0% to 4,716,688 units - the current release, not the stale July 2025 -3.5% figure.
Watsco shares fell 15% on the print, so the market's overall read of that release was negative despite the residential volume line.

verdicts.baseline_evidence: Nothing in TTAN's tape reacts to either 29 July print - the 20-day run-up is only -2.58% while the 5-day is -13.66%, so the damage is concentrated in the last week, long after the HVAC prints, and is sector-multiple in character. That means the market has not obviously extrapolated Lennox's residential slump into TTAN, which is what this finding is arguing against; the bear case it rebuts may not be the bear case that is actually in the price.
verdicts.what_would_change_it: Evidence that a broker cut TTAN numbers or estimates explicitly citing the Lennox residential print would make the rebuttal live and drop this toward 50; a July-2026 AHRI release before tonight showing units down would refute the claim outright.

interactions: These are not three findings, they are one thesis - 'the residential trades end market did not weaken in May-July 2026' - read off three public series, and they should be scored as roughly 1.4 independent claims, not 3. TTAN#0 and TTAN#2 rest on the same physical fact: record cooling load is precisely why AHRI June shipments were +21.7% y/y and why Watsco could call the market 'stabilizing', so counting the NOAA record and the Watsco/AHRI series as separate confirmations double-counts the weather. TTAN#1 is the weakest leg and it also partly contradicts the other two: the July construction hiring strength that TTAN#1 celebrates is attributed by its own sources to data-center and power construction, which is the *nonresidential* end market - if that is what drove the JOLTS beat, it is not evidence about residential trades at all, and TTAN#1's mechanism and TTAN#0/#2's mechanism are not the same market. There is also a live tension with the baseline: the priced lean is downside (25d skew +5.14, spot 29% off the 52-week high, 5d -13.66% on no company news), but the identifiable driver of that derating is the 2026 AI-agent repricing of per-seat vertical SaaS, not the trades end market. TTAN#1 leans hardest on the per-technician-per-month seat model at exactly the moment the market is questioning whether that model survives - so a bullish seat-count datapoint is arguing on a variable the multiple has stopped rewarding. Sizing the whole thesis together rather than summing: if all three are correct and none is priced, the mechanical effect is upside to the usage line plus a modest guide raise, worth perhaps +1.5 to +2.0 points of spot against a 10.08% implied move. Summing the three size estimates independently would overstate it by roughly double. Two factual notes for the record: the hunter's '$66.8m non-subscription' arithmetic is right ($58.5m usage + $8.3m professional services) but only the $58.5m usage line is weather-variable, so '~25% of revenue' should be ~22%; and Lennox reported on 29 July, not 30 July.
